name: which is after the fighting and is not a move.
Delos spared
note: Datis anchored off and would not land armed men on the sacred island. The gesture is the record; the course between is not.
says: Datis anchored at Rhenaia across the channel and would not let the ships anchor at Delos. The Delians had already fled to Tenos.

name: Karystos reduced
note: The Euboean towns were taken in turn on the way north.
says: The islands gave hostages and additional forces. Carystos refused both and was besieged until it yielded.

name: Eretria besieged
note: Six days of assault, then the gates opened from inside. The city was burned and its people enslaved.
says: Six days of assault, heavy losses on both sides, then two Eretrians opened the gates from inside.

name: The landing at Marathon
note: HIPPIAS CHOSE THE GROUND. He had been tyrant of Athens and knew the plain was the best cavalry country in Attica.
says: Marathon was the most convenient place in Attica for horsemen, and near Eretria. Hippias was guiding them.

name: The Athenians march out
note: Out to meet a landing rather than waiting behind walls. The road over Pentelikon is not recorded and is not drawn.
says: Ten generals, of whom the tenth was Miltiades. Drawn up in the sacred enclosure of Heracles.

name: The Plataeans come
note: A thousand men, the whole force of a small city, and the only allies to arrive.
says: The Plataians came to their help in a body.

name: The run
note: POSITIONS DERIVED. Herodotus gives a distance and no coordinates.
says: Not less than eight furlongs, and they came on at a run. The Persians charged them with madness which must be fatal — few, and with neither cavalry nor archers.

name: The centre gives way
note: POSITIONS DERIVED. `Inland` is a direction in the passage, not a place.
says: Where the Persians themselves and the Sacans were drawn up the Barbarians were winning, and broke the ranks of their opponents and pursued them inland.

name: The wings turn inward
note: POSITIONS DERIVED. The shape is in the passage; where each wing stood is not.
says: On both wings the Athenians and the Plataians were winning; they left the routed part to fly unmolested, and bringing the two wings together fought those who had broken their centre.

name: The Persians re-embark
note: Seven ships were taken at the water's edge. The rest got away.
says: SEVEN OF THE SHIPS the Athenians got possession of at the water’s edge. The number is the passage’s own.

name: The fleet rounds Sounion
note: Making for an undefended Athens by sea. The course round the cape is the obvious one and IS NOT RECORDED — the zigzag says from here to here.
says: They took the Eretrian captives off the island where they had left them and sailed round Sunion, purposing to arrive at the city before the Athenians.

name: The army marches back
note: THE RACE THAT DECIDED IT. The same men who had just fought, arriving before the fleet could land.
says: The Athenians came back to the city as speedily as they could and arrived before the Barbarians, encamping at Kynosarges.

name: The fleet turns away
note: They lay off Phaleron, saw the army drawn up, and sailed for Asia.
says: They lay off Phaleron, and then sailed away to Asia.
